description:
Welcome to The AI Learning Advantage, a podcast about the rapidly changing world of artificial intelligence, education, future skills, career development, productivity, and intelligent learning.Artificial intelligence is changing how people learn, work, create, solve problems, and build careers. From AI-powered education and personalized learning to AI skills, automation, knowledge work, and the future of employment, the ability to understand and effectively use AI is becoming one of the most important advantages of the modern economy.The AI Learning Advantage explores what this transformation means for students, professionals, entrepreneurs, educators, business leaders, creators, and lifelong learners.Each episode breaks down important developments in artificial intelligence and connects them to practical learning, career, and business outcomes.We explore how AI is changing education, how people can develop future-proof skills, how professionals can use AI to become more productive, and how organizations can build an intelligent workforce.Topics include AI education, AI learning, artificial intelligence, future skills, AI literacy, career development, workplace AI, AI productivity, AI automation, AI tools, AI agents, generative AI, machine learning, digital transformation, intelligent workplaces, entrepreneurship, professional development, and the future of work.The podcast also examines the economic impact of AI.As intelligent systems become increasingly capable, some skills may become less valuable while others become dramatically more important. Knowing how to ask better questions, evaluate information, make decisions, communicate effectively, think strategically, and work with AI systems may become just as important as traditional technical expertise.We explore how individuals and organizations can adapt to this new environment.You'll discover practical strategies for learning AI, developing valuable skills, improving productivity, building AI-powered workflows, understanding emerging technologies, and preparing for the changing job market.We also examine the rise of AI agents and autonomous systems and what they mean for education and professional development.As AI begins performing increasingly complex tasks, the definition of expertise itself is changing. The advantage may shift from simply knowing information to knowing how to apply judgment, context, creativity, strategy, and human insight alongside intelligent machines.Whether you're learning AI for the first time, developing your career, building a business, teaching others, or preparing for the future of work, The AI Learning Advantage provides practical insights designed to help you stay ahead of technological change.This is not simply a podcast about artificial intelligence.It is a podcast about how humans can become more capable in an AI-powered world.

Subscribe to The AI Learning Advantage for conversations and insights about AI education, future skills, intelligent learning, career growth, productivity, technology, and the future of work.

Why? It helps them get past the jargon and into a lived experience they can relate to.

Here's the thing. Most of the charts and people that are most readily available to relate to are famous people. And...even though we may have their accurate chart, we're only able to relate to a FRACTION of how it shows up because, well, for most of them, we never experience the version of them that exists beyond public image.

This podcast changes that. Human Design IRL is a podcast by real women, for real women, about real (badass) women who are passionate, soulful, and spiritually connected.

Every episode I'll introduce you to one of them, and together, we'll explore how their Human Design shows up in everyday life.

Grounded, honest, and deeply rooted in our local soil, Alamance County Life offers a thoughtful, unfiltered look at the milestones, conflicts, and human stories that forged our home. Subscribe today and join us as we uncover the true history lying just beneath our feet.

title: Stopping Ebola: Inside the Response
author: IIHA Fordham University
description:
The 2026 Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is the fastest growing outbreak on record. It is also taking place in an area of persistent humanitarian crisis. To successfully bring the outbreak under control requires an alliance of community, national leadership, and international solidarity that brings together public health and humanitarian responses. This podcast is a real-time exchange documenting the fast-moving response in DRC. It explores frontline operations, science, policy, humanitarianism, and solutions with some of the world’s most respected experts and strategists on outbreaks and humanitarian action. 

Each episode examines a different aspect of the response and what is required to stop transmission and save lives within a broader humanitarian crisis. Hosted by Ruth Mukwana and Julien Harneis, Senior Ebola Coordinator in Bunia, DRC, the series is produced by the Institute of International Humanitarian Affairs at Fordham University.

You will also learn about image-guided testing and treatments such as prolotherapy, PRP, and bone marrow procedures.

title: Podcasting Social Justice: Dialoges of Resistances
author: Dr Roberto Kulpa & Dr Adrianna Zabrzewska
description:
Welcome to Podcasting Social Justice: Dialogues of Resistances — a podcast series about ‘anti-gender’, a complex, multi-sided political and civil society movement threatening gender and sexual diversity.


In each episode, we look at how campaigns against gender and sexual equality take shape in different places, how these ideas travel across borders and across party lines, and what they mean for everyday life. Along the way, we ask how these debates affect democracy and rights, from education and the media to academic freedoms, reproductive justice, and people’s ability to live and self-identify in safety.


Across the episodes, we not only diagnose what is currently happening but also discuss how we may resist these ‘anti-gender’ mobilisations. You will hear from researchers as well as from feminist and queer organisers and collectives - together, these conversations map the solidarities and strategies that can help sustain pro-equality changes.

***

This podcast series is based on the RESIST Project (2022-2026) (https://theresistproject.eu/) which examined ‘anti-gender’ politics and populisms as well as queer-feminist responses to these illiberal attacks on democracy. The study was conducted across several country cases: Belarus, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Poland, Spain, Switzerland, the EU, as well as a transnational case of people living in exile in Europe. In the project, we have collaborated with 40 advocacy groups, experts, and public intellectuals (e.g. journalist, doctors, artists) to create space for shared learning and grounded knowledge that amplifies those voices who are too often pushed to the margins.

title: One God and savior
author: Jason Turmis
description:
Good morning, I'm Jason Turmis student in Negros fellowship Baptist Seminary 3rd year
This is the first practicum in technology in church ministry

- hear the word “love” every day—in songs, in stories, in families. But so many feel unloved, empty, or like they have to earn love to be accepted.
-
Adlaw-adlaw naton nabatian ang tinaga nga “gugma”—sa mga kanta, sa mga istorya, kag sa mga pamilya. Pero madamo ang nagabatyag nga wala sila ginahigugma, wala sing pulos, ukon daw kinahanglan pa nila nga magpanikasog para lang batunon sang iban.

- Today we look at the only love that never fails, never changes, and never runs out: God’s love for you.

- “Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God… God is love.” — 1 John 4:7–8


1. This love is not earned—it is given
Ini nga gugma wala ginapangabudlayan—ini ginahatag lang

- Most love in the world says: “I love you if… you are good enough, you give me something, you please me.”

Kalabanan nga gugma sa kalibutan nagasiling: “Ginahigugma ko ikaw kon… maayo ka, kon may ginahatag ka sa akon, ukon kon gina dayaw mo ako.”

- But God’s love says: “I love you… period.” He loved you while you were still a sinner (Romans 5:8).

- Greek note: The love described here is agapē—selfless, sacrificial, unconditional love that seeks only your good, never what it can get in return.

2. This love was proven at the cross
Ini nga gugma napamatud-an didto sa krus

- “For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son…” (John 3:16)

- He did not just say He loves you—He gave the most precious thing He had to save you.


- No mistake, no failure, no past can ever make Him stop loving you.

3. This love changes us and flows through us
Ini nga gugma nagabag-o sa aton kag nagaagay sa aton

- “Since God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.” (1 John 4:11)

- When you truly receive His love, you do not just keep it—you share it: with your family, your neighbors, even those who are hard to love.
Kon matuod mo nga nabaton ang Iya gugma, indi mo lang ini pag-ipungot—ipapasa mo ini: sa imo pamilya, sa imo mga kaingod, kag bisan sa mga tawo nga budlay higugmaon.

- We love because He first loved us.
Nagahigugma kita tungod Siya ang una nga naghigugma sa aton.
 

CONCLUSION

- You do not have to prove yourself worthy—He already loves you completely.

Wala ka na kinahanglan magpamatuod nga takos ka—ginahigugma ka na Niya sing bug-os.

- Open your heart to Him today; let His love fill you and lead you.
-
Buksi ang imo tagipusuon sa Iya subong; tuguti ang Iya gugma nga magpuno kag maggiya sa imo.

Serving short stacks and big dreams 🥞☕

Welcome to Milk Money, a podcast for moms who love their kids fiercely AND have dreams, ambitions, identities, and lives of their own. Because motherhood is already a full-time job, but for a lot of us, it isn't the only thing we want to be.

Milk Money is where we talk about the part of motherhood that doesn't always make it into the polished Instagram posts: building a business while raising kids, wanting an identity outside of motherhood, navigating mom guilt, protecting your time and energy, and figuring out how to build a life that actually works for the woman living it.

Whether you call yourself a mompreneur, mom entrepreneur, working mom, business owner, founder, or just a mom who has a little voice saying there has to be more, we saved you a seat.

Meet Your Hostess

I'm Stephanie Lemes — mom, wife, business owner, creative, and the woman behind the mic. I started Milk Money because I was searching for the podcast I needed in this season of my life and couldn't find it.

There were plenty of business podcasts for women. Plenty of motherhood podcasts. But I wanted the conversations that lived in the messy middle — what happens when you're building a business, raising tiny humans, figuring out who you are, and trying not to lose yourself somewhere along the way.

So I decided to create the booth I couldn't find.

Milk Money is for the mom who loves being a mom and still wants something that's hers, is building a business between school drop-off, nap time and bedtime, has big dreams but limited time and energy, or simply wants honest conversations about motherhood and entrepreneurship instead of another highlight reel.

You don't need a six-figure business. You don't need to have it all figured out. You just need to know there's more to your story.

Every week, we're pulling up a chair for honest, unfiltered conversations about motherhood, ambition, business, identity, relationships, health, money, and all the messy bits in between. You'll hear from moms building businesses in all kinds of seasons and stages — and hopefully leave each episode feeling a little less alone.

Because sometimes the best thing another mom can give you isn't advice. It's proof that you're not the only one.

Welcome to the Diner.

Picture a retro roadside diner — checkered floors, coffee refills, chrome, cherry-red booths, jukeboxes, and a bell letting everyone know your order is up.

Why a diner? Because diners are open 24/7, just like motherhood.

There is no clocking out. No true off-shift. So at Milk Money, we're flipping the script: the women doing all the serving finally get to sit down.

Pull up a seat. Stay awhile. Pour it all out.

We'll talk about the wins, the doubts, the pivots, the guilt, the ambition, the chaos, and the dreams that didn't disappear when you became a mom. Expect guest conversations, solo episodes, listener questions, and eventually a phone line where you can call in, ask a question, vent, or just say the thing you haven't been able to say anywhere else.

Because this booth is yours, too.

Milk Money: Serving short stacks and big dreams.

Welcome in, we saved you a seat.

title: Prime Your Health - The Grey Zone
author: Dr. J
description:
I’m Dr. J, a practicing urgent care physician with more than 11 years of experience—and over those years, I’ve noticed something concerning.

We have more health information at our fingertips than ever before, yet people are more confused about their health than ever.

That’s because so much of health lives in what I call the “gray zones.”

The gray zones are the everyday health questions where people need more clarity:

Should I go to urgent care or the ER?
How do I know if a sinus infection needs treatment?
Does this cut need stitches?
When should I worry about a fever?
When is it safe to wait—and when could waiting make things worse?
What should I know before considering vitamins, peptides, weight-loss therapies, or other emerging treatments?

There are thousands of opinions online, but much of that information isn’t coming from physicians who are actively seeing patients and dealing with these questions every day.

That’s why I created this podcast.

In addition to practicing urgent care medicine, I own an IV vitamin therapy and wellness clinic where I’ve gained firsthand experience with IV therapies, vitamins, weight-loss medications, peptides, and other approaches people are increasingly hearing about. I’ve seen what these therapies can do, where they may have limitations, the side effects and risks that need to be considered, and—most importantly—the questions you should be asking before making decisions about your health.

This podcast is about giving you clarity in the gray zones of health.

I’m not here to diagnose or treat you through a podcast. I’m here to help you better understand your body, recognize when something may require medical attention, know where to go for care, understand your options, and ask better questions when making decisions about your health.

My goal is simple: to help you become more informed, more confident, and better prepared to take an active role in your health.

If you’ve ever thought, “I just wish a doctor would explain this in a way that actually makes sense,” you’re in the right place.

The HOPE Podcast — Helping Others Prosper Eternally


The HOPE Podcast is more than a podcast — it is a community platform built to amplify real stories, provide real tools, and inspire real action.


Rooted in the belief that stronger communities are built when people feel seen, heard, supported, and empowered, The HOPE Podcast brings together community leaders, entrepreneurs, artists, athletes, educators, advocates, creatives, and everyday people whose experiences can help someone else move forward.


Hosted by community leader and Neighborhood Star Foundation founder Levar “Calliope Var” Elzy, HOPE creates honest conversations around the issues that affect our communities — mental and emotional well-being, family, business, financial literacy, creativity, relationships, violence, opportunity, leadership, healing, culture, and personal growth.


But the conversation is only the beginning.


HOPE stands for Helping Others Prosper Eternally, and our mission is to turn stories into tools and conversations into action. We don’t simply want to talk about what’s wrong in our communities. We want to highlight the people doing the work, connect people with resources and opportunities, celebrate progress, challenge stigma, and show what’s possible when a community comes together.


Every episode is built around impact. Our guests share not only what they have accomplished, but what they have survived, learned, overcome, and what they are doing to help the next person.


Through storytelling, community engagement, live events, creative initiatives, partnerships, and service, The HOPE Podcast connects the microphone to the streets and the conversation to the community.


We’re not chasing content.


We’re documenting impact, sharing knowledge, amplifying voices, and building HOPE — one story, one resource, one opportunity, and one community at a time.


H.O.P.E. — Helping Others Prosper Eternally.
